strings.disc_entry_sub: 'Recording → speech recognition → optional model processing → typed into your PC'
strings.disc_lead: 'Who sits between your phone microphone and the PC text box is decided by the engine you chose; the program never substitutes another one.'
strings.disc_s1_body: 'While you hold the talk button, your phone captures audio and streams it as you speak; it is never written into our database.'
strings.disc_s2_body: 'Which engine hears you is a visible setting, not a guess: the engine your settings name for the language; failing that, the catch-all engine; failing that, the platform-managed default; failing that, the two engine routes we seeded for you at first boot. If none of those exists either, transcription stops with an error — audio is never quietly sent somewhere else.'
strings.disc_s2_cloud: '· The built-in cloud engine: audio streams through our relay to Soniox. If they are unavailable we may switch this step back to speech-recognition servers we operate. Switching is an operator action — it never re-routes mid-sentence. Audio is held in memory only, never written to disk.'
strings.disc_s2_byok: '· An engine you configured with your own key: audio goes to that provider under their privacy policy, with your credentials. Through the cloud, audio still passes our relay (in memory, never stored). On your own network we are not in the path.'
strings.disc_s2_local: '· A local engine: nothing leaves your own hardware at this step — that is about your voice; where the text goes next is step 3. (You supply the speech model for the built-in engine yourself; it downloads one over the internet only if you explicitly set FLOWMIC_SHERPA_AUTO_DOWNLOAD=1 on the computer.)'
strings.disc_s3_body: 'Translate and Organize always use the language model. Realtime depends on the “AI polish” switch under Settings → Speech recognition (that row is the current value): while it is on, the closing transcript of each recording is sent once — including “Record only”; while it is off, Realtime sends no text. Provisional words are never sent. Whatever is sent goes to the model endpoint your settings name. The platform language model is run by DeepSeek on our account. We retain neither the input nor the output.'
strings.disc_s4_title: '4. Delivered to your PC and typed into the focused box'
strings.disc_s4_body: 'Text is delivered to the computer you paired with and typed into the focused box, via your own network or our cloud relay (which passes frames on and forgets them).'
strings.disc_s4_lan_plain: '⚠️ Whether the local-network route is encrypted depends on how the pairing was made. A QR pairing is encrypted whenever that code carries the identity of the computer; the phone checks it on every later connection. Pairings created before this encryption existed are still in the clear — pairing again on the phone upgrades one. Which of them this connection is, is answered under “Connection encryption” on the phone. The relay is TLS. Setting FLOWMIC_LAN_TLS to 0 on the computer switches encryption off: phones already paired under encryption can no longer connect. Recovering means deleting the computer on the phone and pairing again.'
strings.disc_s5_body: 'We do not store your transcripts; the timeline lives on your phone and your computer. We store your account, paired devices, synced settings, and monthly usage totals (never the content).'
